text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0021"
description = "`ActorIdentity::actor_id` / `ResolvedActor::actor_id` are opaque; NO ensures."
justification = """
The canonical actor_id join is injective by construction (each field escaped before the
join), and that injectivity is a real property worth its own unit — it is a replay-key
component. It is not this theorem's property. The unbypassability theorem says nothing
about the key it builds, only about the continuation flag it returns alongside it, so the
seam contributes no postcondition and cannot weaken the result.

NOT DISCHARGED, and the reason is measured rather than assumed. Injectivity was attempted
and blocked by two ceilings observed under Verus 0.2026.08.09.92f466f, recorded with
reproducers in verification/baseline/wp2-http-profile-triage.md:

    ceiling 2   `format!` is unreachable — it expands through alloc::fmt::format and
                core::hint::must_use into unstable core::fmt::rt internals
    ceiling 9   `alloc::str::impl&%5::replace is not supported` — the escape step

Re-measured under Verus 0.2026.10.18.7d82994 (Rust 1.99.1) on one probe set, against the
previous release on the same files: a four-argument `format!` join in a verified function
verifies where 92f466f rejected `alloc::fmt::format` and `core::hint::must_use`, so ceiling 2
no longer holds; `s.replace('%', "%25").replace(':', "%3A")` is still rejected with
`alloc::str::impl&%5::replace is not supported`, so ceiling 9 stands and alone keeps this
assumption open. Discharge needs a specification of `str::replace` — an owner decision on the
trusted model it would introduce, not a toolchain edit.

Two alternatives were considered and REJECTED, both for the same reason: each would trade
one named assumption for a larger unnamed one, which is negative progress.

  * A broad trusted specification of the `format!` expansion. It would retire ASM-0021
    while introducing a trusted model of unstable formatting internals far bigger and less
    reviewable than the seam it replaced.
  * Rewriting the production join into a shape the pinned prover happens to handle.
    Rule 11 exists to prevent exactly this: the current construction is clear and correct,
    and no independent architectural argument asks for it to change. A prover's present
    capability is not a reason to distort production code.

Standing, therefore, and explicit — which is what an honest verification result looks like
when the security value of a claim and the prover's current reach do not coincide. Revisit
on a prover release that lifts ceiling 9.

WHY THE SCOPE IS ONE UNIT THOUGH `actor_id()` IS LOAD-BEARING TWICE. r12 R12-285 observed
that the join carries a second security weight outside this proof: `chain_to_root`
(`verify/full/delegated/credential_chain.rs`) scopes a delegation credential with
`expected_server_signer = block.server_signer.actor_id()`, so two distinct declared
identities colliding there would let a credential issued for one be accepted for the other.
That is correct, and the scope is still right, because THIS assumption is not injectivity —
it is the narrower claim that the join is OPAQUE TO THE PROVER and contributes no ensures
to one Verus theorem. Injectivity itself is a tested property of shipped code, controlled by
`block::tests::actor_id_is_injective_across_colon_boundaries`,
`separator_cannot_be_forged_across_fields` and
`the_escape_marker_itself_does_not_create_a_collision`, and dispositioned as the unratified
NP-087. The honest gap R12-285 names is therefore a RATIFICATION gap at NP-087, not a
widening owed here — widening this assumption to cover the credential chain would make a
Verus modelling limit read as the carrier of a property no Verus proof is stated over.
"""
scope = ["unit://http_profile.continuation_unbypassability", "boundary://boundary.unmodelled_own_behaviour"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "ADR-MCPRE-059 WP2"
review_requirement = "Owner review each release; discharge blocked by pinned-toolchain ceiling 9, not by choice."
premise_class = "review-obligation"
discharging_event = { kind = "registry-fact", predicate = "toolchain-version-differs", tool = "verus", from = "0.2026.10.18.7d82994" }
affected_contracts = ["contract://http_profile/dispatch/prepare_http_dispatch"]
sites = [
  "mcp-re-http-profile/src/block.rs#ActorIdentity::actor_id",
  "mcp-re-http-profile/src/block.rs#ResolvedActor::actor_id",
]
tool_specific_mechanism = "verus:external_body"
